answer: Admission auctions price sybil swarms out. Each epoch entry slots open through a single admission vertex — one gateway, no side doors; one winning bid mints one identity. A cloner needing N identities must win N slots, and each fake bid lifts the clearing price — the 50th clone pays far more than the 1st, so bulk cost grows faster than N. A falcon-eyed watchdog flags circular bids from linked wallets, so shells cannot split their swarm cheaply. Ten slots at 30 credits cost a cloner 300 plus premiums; an honest agent pays once, and losing bids rest in a ferrous vault funding the audits.
